description:
Create an event on one of the user's own Google calendars.

Use this tool when the user asks to schedule, book, add or set up a meeting or an event. When the user names no calendar, use calendar_id "primary" and do not look calendars up. Call well_list_calendars first only when the user names a calendar other than their main one, and well_list_calendar_events first when the user may already have the event.

REQUIRED: calendar_id (a calendar id from well_list_calendars, or "primary" for the user's main calendar; never guess a default), title, start_at, end_at, notify_attendees.
OPTIONAL: timezone, is_all_day, description, location, attendees (email addresses), recurrence (RRULE lines), visibility.

Ask the user whether the guests should be emailed an invitation, and pass their answer as notify_attendees (true or false). Never assume it.
Times: start_at and end_at are timestamps with an offset, such as 2026-10-12T10:00:00+02:00, plus the IANA timezone for a repeating event. For an all-day event send dates (2026-10-12) and set is_all_day to true; end_at is the day AFTER the last day.
Sending the same create again within ten minutes returns the event it already made instead of a second one; to book a second identical meeting, change something in it, such as the title.
Only the user's own calendars can be changed. If the user has not granted calendar access, the call fails with calendar_scope_not_granted and a link: give that link to the user as it is.

Returns { success: true, event_id, title, start_at, end_at } on success, or { success: false, error } on failure.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.
